item.title: Tragedy in remote PNG: Premature triplets die before Medevac reaches mother
item.description: A remote Markham woman has been flown to Lae for treatment after giving birth to premature triplets, who all died before an emergency evacuation could reach her. The mother was evacuated from the Onga-Waffa local level government area by Manolos Aviation and arrived in Lae shortly after 10am today.
item.content:encoded:
A remote Markham woman has been flown to Lae for treatment after giving birth to premature triplets, who all died before an emergency evacuation could reach her.

The mother was evacuated from the Onga-Waffa local level government area by Manolos Aviation and arrived in Lae shortly after 10am today.

The babies were born at about eight months of pregnancy and died within hours of each other despite efforts by health workers at the local facility.

Manolos Aviation chief executive and pilot Captain Jurgen Ruh said one baby died last night, while the other two died at about 9am today.

“None of the babies survived. One of the babies died last night and the other two died this morning at nine o’clock,” captain Ruh said.

He said the outcome may have been different if the emergency call had reached the evacuation team earlier.

The case highlights the difficulty of providing emergency maternal and newborn care in remote communities, where patients can be hours away from hospitals with specialised facilities.

The mother was brought to Lae for further medical treatment following the loss of her three babies.

The evacuation was carried out under Manolos Aviation’s MAMA Medevac program, which provides emergency air transport for patients in isolated parts of the country.

item.title: Samarai-Murua MP delivers medical supplies
item.description: Samarai-Murua MP Isi Henry Leonard has delivered basic medical supplies to Misima District Hospital, emphasizing that access to essential medicine is critical as the district faces the impacts of El Niño. Leonard presented the supplies during the country’s 51st Independence Anniversary celebrations at Bwagoia station on Misima Island.
item.content:encoded:
Samarai-Murua MP Isi Henry Leonard has delivered basic medical supplies to Misima District Hospital, emphasizing that access to essential medicine is critical as the district faces the impacts of El Niño.

Leonard presented the supplies during the country’s 51st Independence Anniversary celebrations at Bwagoia station on Misima Island.

Misima District Hospital is among numerous health facilities across Papua New Guinea facing severe drug shortages.

The nationwide crisis has forced many hospitals and health centers to scale down operations, attend only to severe cases, and direct patients to purchase drugs at commercial pharmacies.

Leonard said his district administration stepped in to ensure local health facilities received urgent support.

"I am not shy to mention this, because it leads us to step up and continue supporting this hospital. We need to transform it into a proper facility," the local MP said.

"For now, we are delivering what this aircraft can carry. We have basic drugs here to support our patients and the community within the district."

Deputy District Health Administrator Serah Joseph thanked the MP for the intervention, stating that acquiring medicine through standard government procurement channels remains difficult.

"Drugs have been an ongoing problem nationwide. Even through normal processes of getting it from the government, it is really challenging," Ms Joseph said.

Leonard reaffirmed that healthcare remains a top priority for the Samarai-Murua District Development Authority [DDA], pledging continued support to ensure residents have access to basic healthcare.

item.title: 43 children screened for heart issues in Rabaul
item.description: Forty-three children aged between three months and 20 years were screened during a two-day cardiac clinic in Rabaul, marking the largest turnout in the region for the National Cardiac Screening Flying Doctors Program. The two-day visit to Nonga General Hospital by the Operation Open Heart Foundation [OOHF] team concluded the program’s 2026 calendar.
item.content:encoded:
Forty-three children aged between three months and 20 years were screened during a two-day cardiac clinic in Rabaul, marking the largest turnout in the region for the National Cardiac Screening Flying Doctors Program.

The two-day visit to Nonga General Hospital by the Operation Open Heart Foundation [OOHF] team concluded the program’s 2026 calendar.

Out of the 43 patients assessed, 13 were cleared of heart issues, while seven have been put forward for discussions regarding potential open-heart surgery.

Nonga General Hospital Paediatrician in Charge, Dr Veronica Kalit, said clinical diagnoses provided critical pathways for young patients requiring surgery.

"We see them, we diagnose them clinically, but to get a definite diagnosis is helpful, because then you have cases that can actually go for operation," Dr Kalit said. "Every year we have two to four patients that go and have heart operations, and it makes a difference so they can go on to live normal lives."

Six children were diagnosed with Tetralogy of Fallot [ToF], a congenital heart defect present from birth that restricts oxygen flow to the body and causes patients to turn blue.

Dr Kalit said ToF cases were surprisingly common in the area, adding that surgical treatment for the condition is no longer available in Papua New Guinea. This leaves overseas medical travel as the only option for affected families, many of whom cannot afford it.

Senior Paediatrician at Port Moresby General Hospital, Dr Diana Olita’a, who conducted the screening, urged parents and health workers to watch for warning signs rather than mistaking them for routine chest infections.

"A child who is small for age, breathless, easily tired, frequently blue, or has difficulty feeding may have a heart problem," Dr Olita’a said. "They should get their hearts checked."

The medical team also flagged cases of pulmonary hypertension, a severe condition involving high blood pressure in the arteries between the heart and lungs. Left undiagnosed, conditions like ToF, Ventricular Septal Defect [VSD], Atrial Septal Defect [ASD], or Patent Ductus Arteriosus [PDA] can lead to irreversible damage to lung blood vessels.

Travel costs and long distances remain a major barrier to follow-up care for families in East New Britain and across the country.

"The distance they have to travel, the number of buses they have to get on, and the money spent becomes a hindrance," Dr Kalit said.

Despite the challenges, three post-operative patients returned for review during the clinic - two after PDA ligation and one following ASD repair - and were reported to be thriving.

The foundation acknowledged Air Niugini, BSP Limited, the Sir Brian Bell Foundation, and the East New Britain Provincial Health Authority for supporting the regional screening program.

item.title: PNG generates K1.8b cocoa revenue
item.description: Papua New Guinea generated more than K1.8 billion in cocoa export revenue last year following total production of 61,000 tonnes, Agriculture Minister John Boito says. Speaking at the recent launch of the 2026–2035 Cocoa Industry Strategic Plan in Port Moresby, Boito said PNG currently supplies two per cent of the global cocoa market, supporting over 200,000 households and roughly three million peo
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea generated more than K1.8 billion in cocoa export revenue last year following total production of 61,000 tonnes, Agriculture Minister John Boito says.

Speaking at the recent launch of the 2026–2035 Cocoa Industry Strategic Plan in Port Moresby, Boito said PNG currently supplies two per cent of the global cocoa market, supporting over 200,000 households and roughly three million people nationwide.

"In 2025 alone, our country produced more than 61,000 tonnes, generating more than K1.8 billion in export revenue," Boito said. "We should reach K2 billion."

He said smallholder farmers directly received more than 80 per cent of those export earnings.

"With over 80 per cent going directly into the pockets of our farmers and families, cocoa is a lifeline that pays for school fees, funds healthcare, builds homes, and provides a pathway to live with dignity," Boito said. "That is why the future of cocoa must remain an urgent national priority."

Cocoa Board of PNG chief executive Jesse Anjen said high global prices over the past several years have driven increased demand for industry extension services across the country.

"As you can see, over the last two to three years, a lot of exciting things have been happening," Anjen said. "There is a huge demand for cocoa extension services across the country. The prices are really good, and farmers are enjoying the benefit of their labor."

item.title: Marape calls for peace at UN Assembly
item.description: Speaking at the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York last week, Prime Minister James Marape called on world leaders to put human welfare ahead of war and narrow geopolitical interests. He urged leaders to choose dialogue and peaceful means to settle disputes and added that decisions made in one country can affect people thousands of kilometers away.
item.content:encoded:
Speaking at the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York last week, Prime Minister James Marape called on world leaders to put human welfare ahead of war and narrow geopolitical interests.

He urged leaders to choose dialogue and peaceful means to settle disputes and added that decisions made in one country can affect people thousands of kilometers away.

‘’Pollution carried by oceans does not stop at migration points. Wars can disrupt food, fuel, energy, trade, supply chains, far from the battlefield," Marape said.

"Economic decisions made in the world’s largest economy can reach an ordinary family in a small developing country."

He said leaders must remember ordinary families when making major economic decisions, balance commercial interests with the welfare of people, protect our planet while pursuing development, and put the interest of our children’s future generations at the heart of decisions we make today.

Marape said PNG does not claim to have all the answers and that we are still a developing nation.

‘’Few years ago, the country became a middle-income nation. We have our own challenges, but our position as a pacific nation allows us to remind the larger powers of a simple reality, and that is, no nation is so powerful that it can live apart from the earth," he said.

He further stated that no nation is so small that its people should be forgotten when decisions affecting humanity are made.

item.title: Indonesian navy hospital ship rescues 11 PNG nationals stranded at sea
item.description: Eleven Papua New Guineans, including two children, were rescued in the Pacific Ocean early Sunday morning after their boat engine failed, leaving them adrift in open waters. The group was saved by the crew of the Indonesian Navy hospital ship KRI dr. Wahidin Sudirohusodo-991 [KRI WSH-991], which was en route to Vanuatu as part of the 2026 Integrated Port Visit Task Force mission.
item.content:encoded:
Eleven Papua New Guineans, including two children, were rescued in the Pacific Ocean early Sunday morning after their boat engine failed, leaving them adrift in open waters.

The group was saved by the crew of the Indonesian Navy hospital ship KRI dr. Wahidin Sudirohusodo-991 [KRI WSH-991], which was en route to Vanuatu as part of the 2026 Integrated Port Visit Task Force mission.

The rescue unfolded between 12:30am and 2:30am local time on September 27, approximately 11 nautical miles southwest of Green Island. An Officer of the Watch spotted distress signals flashed from a handheld light in the distance, prompting ship commander Colonel Benedictus Hery Murwanto to immediately deploy medical, security, and response teams.

By 1:02am, the 99-meter naval hospital ship had cut its engines alongside a seven-meter vessel carrying eight men, one woman, and two children.

The passengers had departed Buka Island at 7:00am on Saturday, September 26, bound for Nissan Island, when their outboard motor suffered a mechanical failure. Plagued by worsening sea conditions, the group drifted for hours into the night before spotting the naval vessel.

Upon boarding, medical personnel led by Lieutenant Commander Dr. Chairi examined all 11 individuals. The crew provided the passengers with medical evaluations, food, clean drinking water, dry clothing, blankets, and quarters to rest.

Following the rescue, KRI WSH-991 altered course back toward waters off Buka to facilitate a safe drop-off. Once within cellular range, one of the rescued passengers contacted relatives on shore, allowing navy personnel to hand over the group and their belongings directly to family members.

Indonesian naval leadership emphasized that the operation highlights the country's maritime humanitarian commitments in the region.

"The Indonesian Navy's responsibilities extend beyond safeguarding maritime sovereignty and security to upholding humanitarian values in every mission," said Chief of Staff Admiral Dr. Muhammad Ali.

The KRI WSH-991 has since resumed its voyage towards Vanuatu to continue its South Pacific diplomacy and medical outreach mission.

item.title: Australia and PNG deliver vital water upgrades at Moem Barracks
item.description: Major infrastructure upgrades at Moem Barracks in Wewak are improving essential services for the Papua New Guinea Defence Force [PNGDF] while creating jobs and training opportunities for local workers. Delivered through the Australia-Papua New Guinea Defence Cooperation Program, the works are modernising critical infrastructure that supports the central operations precinct of the PNGDF 2nd Royal P
item.content:encoded:
Major infrastructure upgrades at Moem Barracks in Wewak are improving essential services for the Papua New Guinea Defence Force [PNGDF] while creating jobs and training opportunities for local workers.

Delivered through the Australia-Papua New Guinea Defence Cooperation Program, the works are modernising critical infrastructure that supports the central operations precinct of the PNGDF 2nd Royal Pacific Islands Regiment.

Australian Defence Force [ADF] project supervisor, Warrant Officer Class Two Matthew Pfingst, said the upgrades would strengthen the barracks' long-term capability while providing benefits to the local community.

“This base hasn’t had a secure water supply or sewer network for a number of years, and these upgrades will provide that vital secure water supply,” said WO2 Pfingst. “We have been using civilian contractors to do some of these works in order to increase the capacity and experience of the local workforce and also to inject money and jobs into the area.”

As part of the project, upgrades to the ageing water systems and fire network are being undertaken, including the installation of about five kilometres of new pipeline.

Site supervisor, Sergeant Troy Roseman, said the project builds on a long standing partnership between Australia and Papua New Guinea.

“Australia originally built these barracks, and the work we are doing here continues to build on that relationship,” Sgt Roseman said. “Coming back and doing the maintenance and building new infrastructure helps maintain and continue that relationship.”

Local PNG companies are also delivering key components of the project.

Southern Cross Pumps Foreman Demas Towalaun said working alongside ADF personnel had helped develop the skills of local employees.

“Working with ADF has been really helpful,” Mr Towalaun said. “It gives us the opportunity to work with people above our skill level, and for the local workers it becomes a learning stage for them, to put their hands on deck and learn how to build things like tanks.”

The upgrades demonstrate Australia's ongoing commitment to supporting Papua New Guinea's defence capability, infrastructure development and Pacific-led security priorities. They also reflect the strength of the PNG Australia Alliance, a long-standing partnership built on shared security, economic cooperation and strong people-to-people links between both nations.

item.title: Parkop slams barbaric killing at 8-Mile
item.description: NCD Governor Powes Parkop has condemned the recent killings in Port Moresby, particularly at 8-Mile, describing them as 'barbaric acts' that are unacceptable and cannot be tolerated in the city or the country. His comments follow another gruesome killing last week in which a man was hacked to death with a bush knife, echoing a similar attack the week before.
item.content:encoded:
NCD Governor Powes Parkop has condemned the recent killings in Port Moresby, particularly at 8-Mile, describing them as 'barbaric acts' that are unacceptable and cannot be tolerated in the city or the country.

His comments follow another gruesome killing last week in which a man was hacked to death with a bush knife, echoing a similar attack the week before.

Governor Parkop expressed regret and sadness over the loss of life, stressing that his administration has gone beyond legal and political means to support police in restoring safety and security for residents and visitors.

He highlighted the installation of more than 300 CCTV cameras across the city, equipped with infrared lighting and artificial intelligence capacity, as part of a broader push to strengthen surveillance.

Parkop revealed that a Rapid Response Unit is being established to either prevent crimes or ensure swift arrests when incidents occur.

“I have been pushing for this capacity to be in place as soon as possible, and I want to assure city residents we are almost there,” he said.

The Governor noted that these measures complement existing initiatives, including the funding and deployment of City Wardens, Pom City Watch, and neighborhood watch programs.

Together, these efforts are designed to back up regular police operations and extend security coverage to settlements such as 8-Mile.

“We are determined to bring the highest level of safety and security to Port Moresby,” Parkop affirmed. Meanwhile, police in NCD are yet to establish full details behind the latest killing and have not apprehended suspects.

item.title: PNG PALM scheme workers driving economic growth and stronger communities
item.description: Papua New Guinea’s participation in the Pacific Australia Labour Mobility [PALM] scheme continues to deliver significant economic and social benefits for workers, their families, and communities across the country.
